solicitations.title: Amendment 0001 - Questions and Answers "Enclosure A - 19KU2026Q0013 - AEWA Door & Tile Installation Upgrade project
solicitations.description: Subject: Request for Quotations number RFQ 19KU2026Q0013 - AEWA Door & Tile Installation Upgrade project Enclosed is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) for the AEWA Door & Tile Installation Upgrade project . If you would like to submit a quotation, follow all solicitation instructions, and complete the required portions of the attached document. A site visit has been scheduled for Aug 05, 2026, at 09:30 AM Kuwait local time. For more information, please refer to page 33. Interested contractors are strongly encouraged to attend the scheduled site visit to inspect the premises prior to finalizing their proposals, including the Bill of Materials (BOM) and Bill of Quantities (BOQ). It is the contractor’s sole responsibility to thoroughly assess the site during this visit. Any inaccuracies, omissions, or cost discrepancies in the submitted proposal resulting from failure to inspect the site shall be the contractor’s full responsibility . The U.S. Government intends to award a fixed price contract/purchase order to the responsible company submitting a technically acceptable offer at the lowest price. We intend to award a contract based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if there is a need to do so. Note: Prospective offerors are strongly encouraged, though not required, to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov. Offerors with an active SAM registration need only provide their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number and are not required to complete the information 52.204-90 since relevant information is found in their SAM registration. Offerors without an active SAM registration must complete FAR 52.204-90, Offeror Identification, in Section 5, Representations and Certifications. This information must be updated annually if option years are included in the solicitation or award. Offerors are strongly encouraged to maintain an active SAM account For a quotation to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: SF-1442 (14 through 20c) Section A, Price Section L, Representations, certifications, and other statements of offerors or quoters Information and documentation required by Section J, Attachment A, and all other applicable provisions of this solicitation. Proof of SAM Registration / Unique Entity ID, or if not SAM registered, complete FAR 52.204-90, Offeror Identification, ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The purpose of this amendment 0001 is to post Q&As, revise the Statement of Work (SOW) based on the Questions and Answers (Q&As) and to incorporate the following updated requirements under Paragraphs 3.5.1 and 3.5.3: Paragraph 3.5.1 – Install Exterior Door Paragraph 3.5.1 is revised to include the following glass specification: The glass shall be double-glazed, tempered, Low-E, consisting of 6 mm + 20 mm + 6 mm . The glass shall comply with ANSI Z97.1-1984 safety standards. Paragraph 3.5.3 – Fabricate and Install Transaction Counter Paragraph 3.5.3 is revised to clarify the required countertop finish: The transaction counter shall be provided with a Corian countertop . All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. Submit your quote electronically by email to Kuwait_Solicitation@state.gov. Quotations are due by Aug 16, 2026, at 10:00 am Kuwait local time. No quotes will be accepted after this time. Please enter the title of your email as “ Quote – RFQ _19KU2026Q0013 - AEWA Door & Tile Installation Upgrade .

solicitations.title: J--NWS HVAC PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE (PM) WFO AND NEXRA
solicitations.description: AMENDMENT 0001 (08/11/2026): Add Q&A 1. Subcontractor Past Performance and Technical Experience Evaluation o Context: RFQ Section XII, provisions FAR 52.212-1 and 52.212-2, state that quotes must include at least two references from at least two separate contracts for similar and relevant recent services performed within the past two years to demonstrate capability. Under a prime-subcontractor teaming arrangement, a small business prime contractor manages administration, invoicing, and overall compliance, while a specialized local subcontractor performs physical, on-site technical services. o Question: Will the Government evaluate the past performance, technical experience, and HVAC certifications of proposed key subcontractors to satisfy the evaluation criteria under Technical Acceptability/Capability and Past Performance, provided the subcontractor is clearly identified and a signed teaming agreement or commitment letter is submitted with the quote? o Answer: Yes, subcontractor’s past performance is sufficient. 2. Pricing of Materials, Parts, and Specialty Equipment under Unscheduled Emergency Repair CLINs o Context: Section II, CLINs 0003 and 0004 (and Option Year equivalents) request a firm-fixed hourly rate for unscheduled emergency repairs. SOW Section 2.3.1 states that emergency repairs will include labor, parts, and components required to troubleshoot, diagnose, or repair faulty equipment, and that estimates must be submitted to the TPOC for review. SOW Section 7.0 further states that the contractor shall furnish all materials. o Question: Please clarify how replacement parts, materials, and specialty equipment required for unscheduled emergency repairs should be priced and invoiced under CLINs 0003 and 0004. Are offerors permitted to bill these parts at cost, or with a fixed material markup percentage? Alternatively, should offerors include a standard plug-in material allowance, or is the hourly rate intended to be fully burdened to cover labor only, with parts handled via separate post-award bilateral modifications? o Answer: Unscheduled emergency repairs will require estimates to be submitted to the TPOC for review and approval, using the labor rate provided in the RFP, and the pricing for the parts/components that need to be replaced. We presume the parts portion of the estimates will include a reasonable markup. 3. Specific Manufacturer Models, Types, and Quantities of Backup Batteries o Context: SOW Section 2.1.7 requires the contractor to inspect and replace backup batteries for HVAC controllers and Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) annually. SOW Section 4.6 lists on-site equipment, including Trane UC600 Tracer Controls and Trane PM014 Power Supply Modules, but does not provide specifications or models for the on-site VFDs. o Question: To ensure accurate pricing of materials and avoid system disruptions, could the Government provide the specific manufacturer model numbers, battery types (e.g., lithium coin cells, sealed lead-acid modules), and total quantities of batteries requiring annual replacement for the VFDs and controllers at both the WFO and NEXRAD locations? o Answer: We do not have that information. This is likely a nominal cost. 4. Applicability of Service Contract Act (SCA) Wage Determinations o Context: Section X lists two separate Wage Determinations as contract attachments: Charleston WD 2015-4427 and Hampton WD 2015-4441. The places of performance consist of WFO Charleston (Charleston County) and NEXRAD Early Branch (Hampton County). o Question: Please confirm the geographic applicability of each Wage Determination. Is it the Government’s intent that WD 2015-4427 applies strictly to work performed at the Charleston WFO, and WD 2015-4441 applies strictly to work performed at the NEXRAD site in Early Branch? o Answer: Wage Determination is correct to the best of our knowledge. 5. Scope Clarification on Scheduled Consumables vs. Emergency Repair Parts o Context: SOW Section 2.1.5 and 2.1.6 mandate the annual replacement of the 3M HF60-S water filter cartridge and the Nortec humidifier steam cylinder (Nortec model 202). SOW Section 7.0 requires the contractor to furnish all materials. o Question: Please confirm that the cost of procuring and installing the Nortec 202 steam cylinders and 3M HF60-S water filter cartridges must be fully absorbed within the scheduled PM CLINs (CLIN 0001, etc.), rather than billed separately under CLIN 0003. Additionally, are there any other specialty HVAC consumables (excluding standard belts and MERV air filters) that must be replaced on a routine, scheduled basis? o Answer: Factored into the CLIN 0001 price. There are no other specialty HVAC consumables. 6. Site Visit Coordination and Quote Deadline Extension Request o Context: Solicitation 1305M326Q0394 was issued on August 3, 2026, with questions due by August 10, 2026, and quotes due on August 14, 2026. SOW Section 2.0 strongly encourages a pre-proposal site visit and emphasizes that field verification takes precedence over SOW discrepancies. WFO Charleston and remote NEXRAD Early Branch are geographically separated by approximately 80 miles, and site access requires physical LPOC escorts. o Question: To allow offerors sufficient time to coordinate and conduct site visits across both geographically separated secure facilities, perform necessary field verifications, and compile highly accurate, non-reiterative technical packages with local technical teams, will the Government consider extending the quote submission deadline by one week, to August 21, 2026? o Incumbent Contractor: Could you please confirm whether there is a current incumbent for this contract? If so, we would appreciate it if you could share the associated Purchase Order number and the total contract value. o Answer: No incumbent new requirement and we will not be extending solicitation date. END OF AMENDMENT 0001 REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ) NWS HVAC PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE (PM) TWO LOCATIONS WFO AND NEXRAD IN SOUTH CAROLINA. 1. Solicitation number 1305M326Q0394 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ), for National Weather Service HVAC Preventive Maintenance (PM) two (2) Locations; WFO in Charleston, SC and NEXRAD in Early Branch, SC. Services, non-personal, to provide all labor, equipment and materials (unless otherwise provided herein) necessary for HVAC Systems Preventative Maintenance at Weather Forecast Offices (WFO) in Charleston, SC and Next Generation Radar (NEXRAD) locations in Early Branch, SC in accordance with the Statement of Work. See attached Statement of Work which applies to Base Year and all Option Years 1 – 4. A complete description of requirements for the items to be acquired, including documentation supporting any brand name descriptions or technical data, can be found in the SF18. 2. This is a request for quotations (RFQ) for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Government intends to award a low priced, technically acceptable, single firm fixed-price purchase order on an all or none basis with payment terms of Net 30. 3. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. Department of Labor Wage Rates which can be found on: https://sam.gov/content/wage-determinations or on attachments of this solicitation. THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT ACCEPT RESPONSIBILITY FOR NON-RECEIPT OF QUOTES. IT IS THE CONTRACTOR’S RESPONSIBILITY TO REQUEST AND RECEIVE A CONFIRMATION OF THE QUOTE RECEIPT. solicitations.description: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Emergency Temporary Roofing Program Request for Information (RFI) 70FBR926I00000001 REQUEST FOR INFROMATION (RFI) SUMMARY : The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Emergency Temporary Roofing Program requires supplies for Rota roofing mission due to damage sustained by Super Typhoon Bavi. GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for FEMA’s Emergency Temporary Roofing Program. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research PROPRIETARY INFORMATION AND DISCLAIMERS: Respondents shall identify any proprietary information in their RFI response. Information submitted in response to this RFI will be used at the discretion of the Government. Further, the information submitted will remain confidential insofar as permitted by law, including the Freedom of Information and Privacy Acts. FEMA reserves the right to utilize any non-proprietary technical information in the anticipated PWS or solicitation. Although it is not necessary to address in their response, respondents should be aware of any potential, actual, or perceived organizational conflicts of interest. Any real or potential conflicts must be sufficiently mitigated prior to a contract award. For further guidance, refer to the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Part 9.5. NACIS CODE : 321114, 423310, 423310 PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): 5510 ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE START DATE: August 31, 2026 ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: The Rota roofing mission will be executed in three delivery phases, each tied to a fixed need by date. Materials shall be delivered and ready for use no later than the dates below, with quantities for each phase detailed in the attached schedule. Phase 1: Materials delivered and ready for use no later than August 31, 2026 Phase 2: Materials delivered and ready for use no later than September 7, 2026 Phase 3: Materials delivered and ready for use no later than September 15, 2026 Phased delivery reflects the sequenced nature of the roofing mission in Rota, allowing repair crews to begin work on early-stage structures while later phase materials are still in transit. Failure to meet a phase deadline may impact downstream repair schedules and delay mission completion. RFO RESPONSE SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS: Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Demetria Carter, Contracting Officer, at (demetria.carter@fema.dhs.gov) and Jacob Triplett, Acquisition Procurement Specialist, at (jacob.triplett@fema.dhs.gov) no later than 3:00 PM Chamorro Standard Time (ChST), Wednesday August 12, 2026 .
